issues.explanation: issue_date defaults from issued_at, but an explicitly supplied issue_date (e.g. create(['issue_date' => '2026-09-28']) with the default issued_at = now()) overrides that closure and can leave the row with issue_date out of sync with issued_at, whereas requirement 5 says issue_date must stay aligned for factory-created rows.
The contract asks for a `date` cast; `date:Y-m-d` is a custom_datetime cast that still returns Carbon (so toDateString() works) but adds a serialization format that is not needed.
`$ticket->queue ?? Queue::query()->find($queueId)` can issue an extra Queue query for every factory-made ticket; reusing/associating the resolved queue once would keep the factory leaner.
A global helper function `prefixMapOwner()` is declared in a Pest file; a closure/helper trait would avoid a cross-file redeclaration if another test file ever defines the same name.

down() cannot restore the old (queue_id, code) unique index once the same code exists on more than one day; the comment documents this, but the rollback will fail until duplicates are resolved manually.

review.summary: The change implements priority-derived ticket code prefixes (default N/P/E with range fallback and a validated per-queue override map), moves the sequence to a per-day/per-prefix allocation via a new tickets.issue_date column and 3-column unique index, reads the clock once in IssueTicket, and updates the factory, UpdateQueue, docs and CHANGELOG. The implementation is complete and well tested, including invalid-map, authorization, mass-assignment, midnight and malformed-code cases; the only findings are small nits (factory issue_date/issued_at alignment when issue_date is passed explicitly, the date:Y-m-d cast, an extra queue query in the factory, a global test helper, and the documented rollback caveat), so I would approve with nits.
